# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 62 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 62 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_062_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 8 — What It Means to Defile the Flesh

**62:1** I asked him to explain why the flesh perishes while the soul is saved. "Listen," he said. "Those who have kept their spirit pure from the very beginning, never defiling it — these are the righteous ones. The Lord sees their spirit, approves it, and grants them eternal life."

**62:2** "But those who have honored God's commandment but failed to keep their flesh pure — who defiled it — they will also live, but their life will be somewhat shorter. It's like someone who knows the Lord's commandment but doesn't follow it: they bring the loss on themselves."

**62:3** "Lord," I said, "I still don't follow. What does it mean to defile the flesh?" "Listen," he said. "Departing from God is what defiles the flesh. Anyone who gets involved in the behavior of double-minded people is departing from God and defiling themselves."

**62:4** "Those who live in forgetfulness and deceive themselves through their supposed knowledge will also live — but not with the same life as those who have kept the commandment purely. Those who have departed from God, sinned, and never repented will die. Those who left the angel's presence sorrowfully — they are people who sinned, repented, and will therefore live. But their life will be shortened."

**62:5** When I had taken all this in and understood it, I said: "Lord, what are you really talking about here?" He said: "I'm referring to people who have been called by God's name but have gone astray — seduced by love of wealth, possessions, power, and the emptiness of this world. These are the people who have robbed themselves of God's salvation."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing Hermas's pastoral diagnosis of spiritual self-destruction through worldliness.*
